intro: Detectives read people, solve complex cases and make careful judgments. The closest of the 25 careers below is Coroners, with an 83% skill match, while police and detective supervisors are 81% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $106,040, which is 13% more than the $93,790 detectives earn.
why_it_works: Working a case means interviewing witnesses, testing stories against evidence and writing reports that hold up in court. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 4.12 out of 5 for this job, and judgment and complex problem solving at 3.88. Compliance, fraud and supervision roles use the same skills. About half of the matches need a bachelor's degree. The gaps are managing people and budgets.
tips: Fraud examination is a 73% match and suits detectives with financial case experience.
Air Traffic Controllers earn $148,080, which is 58% more, though entry has strict age rules.
Ask to lead a unit or train new investigators; managing people is your main skill gap.

faq.q: What jobs can former detectives do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Coroners (83%), police and detective supervisors (81%) and Compliance Officers (75%), based on O*NET 31.0. Fraud examiners and analysts are 73% matched, with a median of $81,100 for their broader BLS group, and often hire former investigators.

faq.q: Which careers for detectives pay more?
faq.a: 6 of the 25 matches pay more than $93,790. Air Traffic Controllers earn $148,080 (58% more), Facilities Managers $106,660 (14% more) and police and detective supervisors $106,040 (13% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Controller jobs have strict entry age limits.

faq.q: Do detectives need a degree to change careers?
faq.a: Often. 13 of the 25 matches need no more education than detectives already have, including 5 of the top 10. A bachelor's degree is common in the closest match, held by 35% of workers, and compliance roles usually ask for one.

The skills that most often need work are managing people, managing materials, instructing and managing financial resources. Coordination already rates 3.62 out of 5 for detectives in O*NET, so leading teams and budgets are the main steps toward management roles.
